## ✨ Highlights

- 📦 **Every extension fits again, and every image is smaller**: the root filesystem is built with 1 MiB blocks, about 6 % smaller - 14.96 → 14.10 MiB for the default image, 64.26 → 60.09 MiB with every extension at once. With every extension, v2026.10.14-6 had outgrown the 64 MiB update slots an installed disk has: the image factory couldn't build it. Boot time is unchanged.

## 📦 Images

- **1 MiB squashfs blocks** (zstd, level 19 as before): zstd compresses the big binaries better over a larger window. Measured on v2026.10.14-6's own build inputs with every extension: 64.26 MiB with the previous 128 KiB blocks, 60.09 MiB now. On a real boot (UEFI, KVM), janusd listens 1.2 s after the kernel started with either block size.
- **The update slots are 64 MiB for good**: an installed disk never changes its partitions, so a release can't outgrow them. Every release is now checked with every extension at once: the build fails above 64 MiB, and warns with less than 2 MiB left. The test image called "all extensions" held two of them, so nothing saw v2026.10.14-6 coming.
- **The image factory**: a schematic with every extension builds again from this release. v2026.10.14-6 itself stays too big with every extension - the factory builds a release with its own scripts: use this one.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Nodes**: the usual A/B update. A node on v2026.10.14-6 or older reads the new image like any other: the release it installs, and its other slot, are named as before.
- **The Controller**: nothing changed beyond the version.
- **janusctl**: nothing changed beyond the version.
- **The Terraform provider**: nothing changed.
